newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian barley vote extended for some farmers.
newsitem.headline: Canadian barley vote extended for some farmers.

text.p: The auditors running a plebiscite on whether to end the Canadian Wheat Board's monopoly on western barley exports said on Monday it was extending the vote deadline by a week for some farmers.
"A small group of eligible producers may have been prevented from mailing their ballots on time because they did not receive them soon enough," auditors KPMG said in a statement.
"This group will now have one extra week -- until Friday, March 7, 1997 -- to mail in their ballots in their official return envelopes."
The Alberta Grain Commission had asked the federal government on Friday to extend the deadline because of the difficulty some farmers had had in getting their ballots in time.

KPMG said the new deadline will apply only to farmers who had to file affidavits verifying their eligibility. This applied to producers who did not have a current Canadian Wheat Board Permit Book on or before January 1.
The management firm said the cut-off for filing affidavits was February 18. As affidavits came in to KMPG prior to that date, ballots were sent out.
In total, about 1,700 requests for affidavit forms were sent out, of which 900 were completed and returned, to be added to the voters list and receive ballots.

More than half of these were processed on or before February 18, while others were postmarked only on or shortly before that date, limiting the time for ballots to be returned by February 28. It is only this small group to which the additional voting time applies, KPMG said.
KPMG said it had received more than 55,000 ballots postmarked before February 28 -- 70 percent of those eligible.
"Further envelopes will be received this week from those who mailed them right up against the deadline," it said.
The vote will commence as soon as KPMG is satisfied all outstanding ballots have been returned, including those who from those in the affidavit group who did not receive a ballot on time.
Farmers are being asked whether they wish to be able to sell their export barley on the free market or only through the Canadian Wheat Board.
